findings.excerpt: theorem krawtchouk_eq_zero_of_lt (q n w j : ℕ) (hj : j ≤ n) (hw : n < w) :
findings.problem: The lemma is tagged `@[simp]` but has two non-trivial side conditions, `j ≤ n` and `n < w`. Simp must discharge both before it can rewrite. Neither appears in the LHS `krawtchouk q n w j`, so symbolic arguments only work if the exact hypotheses are in the simp set or context. In the typical use, `j` is bound by `j ∈ range (Fintype.card ι + 1)`. That gives `j < card ι + 1`, not `j ≤ card ι`, so the discharger has no direct way to prove `hj`. The tag therefore adds little, and it puts a rule that mostly fails on its side goals into the default simp set. This is a simp-interface concern.
findings.proposed_change: Remove `@[simp]`, or keep the lemma as a plain theorem that callers invoke explicitly. If a simp form is wanted, state the vanishing with hypotheses that simp can supply, for example `j < n + 1` or `hj : j ∈ range (n + 1)`. Alternatively, add a separate simp lemma for the unconditional case `n < w` with `j = 0`, or one in which `j ≤ n` is replaced by a hypothesis the sum-range context gives.
findings.benefit: The default simp set no longer contains a rule that nearly always fails its side goals. Users get a lemma whose hypotheses match the form in which they appear, namely `Finset.mem_range` bounds on `j`. This avoids attempted discharges at every `krawtchouk` term.
